title: Declare DTOs in contracts/

facts.note: Bun realization; project toolchain is detectable.
Test files and vendored/build directories are never scanned (source exception).
Path-segment conditions only; no file-extension restriction is implied. Files with no layer segment are outside the rule.
Diff-level observer for a coder adding or moving a type whose name ends in `DTO` into a scanned file. Fires the coder-time guidance; it is NOT required for the detector check.
Detector scans all `*DTO` declarations in scanned files, including pre-existing ones. Combination: the rule fires when (change OR finding) holds together with the language/file_kind/path_glob facts.

fires: A coder adds a `*DTO` type in a source file whose path has a layer segment (e.g. a feature's domain, application or infrastructure directory) and no `contracts` segment, in a Bun project.
A coder moves an existing `*DTO` declaration into a layer-segment source file whose path lacks a `contracts` segment.
The detector reports an existing `*DTO` declaration in a layer-segment source file without a `contracts` segment (e.g. one another feature imports, a private type leak).
doesNotFire: A `*DTO` declared in a file whose path contains a `contracts` segment.
A `*DTO` declared in a test file or under a vendored/build directory.
A `*DTO` in a file carrying no layer segment (outside the rules, not in violation).
A type whose name does not end in `DTO`.
A bare npm specifier import (not layer-checked); this does not suppress a finding for a locally declared `*DTO`.

given: A Bun source file with a layer segment and no `contracts` segment in its path
when: a `*DTO` type is declared in or moved into it
then: Declare the `*DTO` type inside a `contracts/` module, not in a feature's internal layer.
prefer: Canonical path: declare the DTO in `contracts/`; import it from both sides of the boundary.
During GREEN: reuse an existing contract type that already represents the payload.
During GREEN: add only fields the current acceptance requires.
During GREEN: create a new DTO only for a genuinely distinct boundary shape.
avoid: Declaring the DTO in a feature layer as a temporary shortcut.
Moving unrelated internal types into contracts.
Another feature importing a DTO declared in one feature's layer (private type leak).
unless: Test files and vendored/build directories are never scanned.
A file with no layer segment is outside these rules, not in violation.
why: A DTO belongs to the contract (owned by neither side), not to either side; inside one feature's layer it becomes a private type others import anyway, so the boundary runs through somebody's internals.
evidence: Every affected DTO declaration lives under `contracts/`.
bun_clean_architecture_detector reports no dto-placement finding for any affected `*DTO` declaration.
verifier_detail: Flags a `*DTO` declaration (type name suffix `DTO`) in a file whose path contains no `contracts` path segment.
contracts_module: a path segment `contracts` — where a boundary shape belongs, since it is owned by neither side.
private_type_leak: a DTO declared inside one feature's layer that another feature imports anyway, running the boundary through somebody's internals.
Test files and vendored/build directories are never scanned.
Bare npm specifiers resolve outside the project graph and are not layer-checked (import-resolution exception; it does not exempt a local `*DTO` declaration).
A file carrying no layer segment is outside these rules rather than in violation of them.
audit: Source name: 'DTOs are declared in contracts/'

strict: fails on every finding; no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.
